case.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
case.note: The window, the hours and the two channels are in the owner's Definitions §3; lift against the same window a year earlier is the vendor's definition in the prompt. The month before gives $4,442 instead of $5,272.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-01: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?

WITH lunch AS (
  SELECT gross_sales_cents, created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago' AS local_time
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND channel IN ('in_store', 'square_online')
)
SELECT sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2026-08-03' AND '2026-08-30')
     - sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2025-08-03' AND '2025-08-30')
FROM lunch
WHERE extract(hour FROM local_time) BETWEEN 11 AND 13

trace.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
trace.answer:
Lunch brought in $1,751.36 more in net sales during Lunch 20 than in the same period last year. The promotion ran Aug 3 to Aug 30, 2026, and I compared it with Aug 3 to Aug 30, 2025 [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion].

The comparison covers lunch only, 11:00 to 13:59 local time [Definitions §2, Lunch]. It includes completed orders in store and on Square Online, the two channels the promotion covered. Net sales are gross sales minus discounts minus refunds.

- **2026:** $34,610.93 net, from 1,414 orders. Gross sales were $40,261.46, discounts were $5,373.26, and refunds were $277.27.
- **2025:** $32,859.57 net, from 1,194 orders. Gross sales were $34,989.77, discounts were $1,497.21, and refunds were $632.99.

Gross sales rose by $5,271.69, but the 20% discount took back most of that. Net sales rose about 5.3%.

case.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
case.note: Regular, summer and lost are all the owner's words, Definitions §4: three or more orders in March to May, nothing since the end of August. 177 of 599.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-03: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?

WITH visits AS (
  SELECT customer_id, (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago')::date AS local_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT count(*)
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM visits
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-05-31') >= 3
     AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day > '2026-08-31') = 0
) lost_regulars

case.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
case.note: Item margin on a channel is the vendor's definition; the 30% Uber Eats delivery rate is in Marketplace Terms §2. Pickled Vegetables at $1.55 a unit, Fried Egg next at $1.61.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-04: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?

SELECT i.name
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND o.channel = 'uber_eats'
  AND o.fulfillment_type = 'delivery'
  AND c.name = 'Sides'
GROUP BY i.name, i.cost_cents
ORDER BY avg(oi.unit_price_cents) * 0.70 - i.cost_cents
LIMIT 1

case.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
case.note: Net payout, the vendor's definition: card fees off in-store orders, 25% commission off DoorDash delivery. $30.11 against $27.47 an order, so $2.64 more in store despite the 25% marketplace markup.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-05: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?

WITH september AS (
  SELECT o.channel, o.fulfillment_type, o.gross_sales_cents,
         o.gross_sales_cents - o.discount_cents AS after_discount,
         coalesce(p.processing_fee_cents, 0) AS fee
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'completed'
  WHERE o.state = 'completed'
    AND date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') = '2026-09-01'
)
SELECT round(
    avg(after_discount - fee) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'in_store')
  - avg(after_discount - gross_sales_cents * 0.25) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'doordash' AND fulfillment_type = 'delivery')
)
FROM september

trace.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
trace.answer:
In September 2026 (completed orders only), we kept about $2.64 more per in-store order than per DoorDash delivery order.

- **In store:** about $30.11 per order across 2,633 orders. This is gross sales minus discounts minus the card processing fee.
- **DoorDash delivery:** about $27.47 per order across 1,269 orders. This is gross sales minus discounts minus DoorDash's 25% commission on delivery orders [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. DoorDash orders carry no processing fee.

DoorDash menu prices already sit 25% above in-store prices [Definitions §5, Marketplaces]. That markup is why the gap is smaller than the commission alone would suggest.

I did not subtract refunds from either figure.

trace.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
trace.answer:
No. Under [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours], no text of any kind can go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If we don't know a customer's local time, we use Central time. A text at 10pm falls inside that window. Send it between 9am and 8pm instead.

Promotional texts also have other rules:
- They can only go to customers with verified SMS consent, and never to anyone who has unsubscribed [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].
- Any discount is capped at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve more. The text must also state an expiry date no more than 14 days out and say "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- The text must name the restaurant and end with "Reply STOP to opt out" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

case.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.

trace.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
trace.answer:
I can't set up this text. The messaging policy rules out both parts of it.

- **Seasonal Specials:** They "may never be discounted in a message" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **25% discount:** Any discount in a text over 20% needs your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

I haven't proposed the campaign or pulled an audience count.

Here are two versions that would fit the rules:
- **Different items:** Offer up to 20% off items other than Seasonal Specials. The offer has to expire within 7 days and apply once per customer.
- **Loyalty message:** Send a stamp-balance or free-drink reminder with no offer in it.

Either way, "regulars" means customers with four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. For a marketing text, they also need an order in the last 90 days and a phone number on file, or verified SMS consent. Anyone who has unsubscribed gets nothing. Customers on the existing-relationship basis can get at most two marketing texts a month [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts; Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency].

Do you want me to draft one of these and propose it for approval?

case.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.

trace.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.
trace.answer:
I proposed a $60.00 comp for table 12, but nothing has happened yet. The proposal is pending, and the owner has to approve it.

The check flagged that $60 is over the $25 manager limit. A manager can comp up to $25 for a food quality complaint like cold pho. Anything above that needs the owner, who can be reached by text during service [House Policy §2, Comps]. The same section says a week's comps should stay under 1% of that week's gross sales.

I couldn't tie the comp to a specific order. The data doesn't record table numbers, and many in-store orders over the last few days total between $50 and $70. The proposal has no order attached. Whoever approves it will need to pick the right ticket, or you can give me the order ID or the time it was rung up.
